name: Method Invocation Quiz
description: A short quiz about how method calls in Python are resolved to the definitions they invoke, based on a small demo program.

questions.text: In the demo program below, which call resolves unambiguously to the method it invokes?
choices: self._check(token)
auth.verify(token)
handle_request(token)
Auth()

questions.text: The demo program calls auth.verify(token), where auth is a local variable. Why can a static analyzer not prove which verify method runs?
choices: The type of auth is not recorded anywhere
verify is a reserved Python keyword
Static analyzers never read function bodies
auth is an imported module
questions.correct_answer: The type of auth is not recorded anywhere

questions.text: When an analyzer cannot resolve a call to a definition, what does it typically record instead?
choices: An unresolved reference to the call symbol
The first definition it happens to find
Nothing at all
A runtime exception
questions.correct_answer: An unresolved reference to the call symbol

questions.text: Which call shapes can a static analyzer usually resolve to an exact definition? Select all that apply.
choices: A bare call to a uniquely named function
self.method() inside a class
instance.method() where instance is a local variable
super().method()
A bare cross-file call to a uniquely named function
correct_answer: A bare call to a uniquely named function
A bare cross-file call to a uniquely named function

questions.text: True or False: a call to self.method() inside a class always refers to a method of that same class.
The formtuitous TUI defines several methods named compose in screens.py and widgets.py. How many compose method definitions exist in total?
One word: what do we call a call whose target an analyzer cannot determine?
The demo program assigns auth = Auth() and later calls auth.verify(token). What extra information would let an analyzer connect auth.verify to Auth.verify?
choices: The type of auth, for example auth: Auth
The line number of the call
The name of the calling function
The return type of verify
questions.correct_answer: The type of auth, for example auth: Auth

questions.text: Suppose several classes each define a method named compose, and a program calls screen.compose(). Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
choices: The call is ambiguous without knowing screen's type
A name-based match credits every compose method
The analyzer can prove exactly which compose runs
Knowing screen's type would resolve the call
correct_answer: The call is ambiguous without knowing screen's type
A name-based match credits every compose method
Knowing screen's type would resolve the call

questions.text: A call-graph diagram of the demo program draws handle_request pointing at an unresolved auth.verify node. Which statement best describes that drawing?
choices: It records the call as a fact and the target as unknown
It proves handle_request never invokes verify
It shows the resolved Auth.verify method
It means the diagram tool has a bug
questions.correct_answer: It records the call as a fact and the target as unknown

questions.text: How confident are you in your answers to this quiz?
